themes_detail.label: For-Hire Vehicle Surge
themes_detail.summary: For-hire vehicle complaints (Uber, Lyft, etc.) spiked to 30 complaints THIS WEEK, more than double the 8-week average of 14.2 weekly complaints—a 110% spike—suggesting either a sudden operational change, surge pricing concentration in the district, or driver conduct issues.
evidence: 30 for-hire vehicle complaints THIS WEEK vs. 14.2 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 5.34)
110% spike represents statistically significant deviation (z-score 5.34, severity: high)
1130 active DOB building permits filed in 90 days suggest heavy construction/delivery traffic may be exacerbating congestion
reporting_angles: Interview residents and businesses in high-complaint areas (Fort Greene Park vicinity, Brooklyn Heights waterfront) about what changed this week—new ride-sharing hub, surge-pricing event, or driver behavior complaints
Contact TLC to cross-reference spike with any new permit issues, driver complaints, or service expansion in CD 302

themes_detail.label: Animals in Parks Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Animal-in-park complaints jumped 300% THIS WEEK to 8 complaints vs. a 2.0 weekly average—the highest statistical anomaly detected (z-score: 5.37)—pointing to either a wildlife incursion, rodent problem, or unsecured food waste in Fort Greene Park.
evidence: 8 animal-in-park complaints THIS WEEK vs. 2.0 weekly average (z-score: 5.37, severity: high)
300% spike is the largest proportional increase among all 311 anomalies detected
Fort Greene Park is major green space serving thousands; spike suggests acute localized problem
reporting_angles: Visit Fort Greene Park and interview park-goers, joggers, dog walkers about what animals they've seen and whether they feel safe
Contact Parks Dept. about recent wildlife reports, trash management changes, or pest control interventions at the park this week

themes_detail.label: Elevator Maintenance Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Elevator complaints surged 227% three weeks ago (27 complaints vs. 8.2 weekly average, z-score: 5.43)—the most sustained high-severity spike—indicating systemic building code or maintenance failures across residential and public buildings in a district with many older mid-rise structures.
evidence: 27 elevator complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 8.2 weekly average (z-score: 5.43, severity: high)
Spike timing suggests systemic issue, not isolated incident
815 active building alterations filed in past 90 days; many older Fort Greene brownstones and Brooklyn Heights towers may have aging elevator infrastructure
reporting_angles: FOIA request to DOB for elevator violations and failed inspections in CD 302 over past 6 months; cross-reference with 311 spike timing
Interview residents in buildings that filed 311 elevator complaints; determine if complaints are about same buildings or district-wide pattern

themes_detail.label: Residential Waste Disposal Surge
themes_detail.summary: Residential disposal complaints jumped 178% THIS WEEK to 8 complaints vs. 2.9 weekly average (z-score: 4.87)—a sudden spike suggesting either bulk collection disruption, new building move-ins creating overflow, or illegal dumping in response to construction activity.
evidence: 8 residential disposal complaints THIS WEEK vs. 2.9 weekly average (z-score: 4.87)
178% spike aligns temporally with surge in for-hire vehicles and animal complaints, suggesting multi-system strain
1130 active DOB permits include 84 new buildings, indicating turnover and possible move-in waste peaks
reporting_angles: Check DSNY schedule for bulk collection changes or service reductions in CD 302 this week
Interview sanitation workers and building superintendents about waste accumulation hot spots

themes_detail.label: Day Care Licensing Concerns
themes_detail.summary: Day care complaints spiked 256% last week to 4 complaints vs. 1.1 weekly average (z-score: 4.8)—a sudden spike that warrants investigation into facility safety, staffing, or regulatory compliance issues affecting young children in this family-dense district.
evidence: 4 day care complaints last week vs. 1.1 weekly average (z-score: 4.8, severity: high)
256% spike suggests either multiple complaints against same facility or district-wide enforcement action
CD 302 (Fort Greene/Brooklyn Heights) is family-oriented neighborhood; potential safety issue affects high-risk population
reporting_angles: FOIA request to NYC Department of Health for day care violations and inspection reports in CD 302 filed in past 4 weeks
Interview parents and staff at facilities receiving complaints; determine if complaints involve licensing, safety, or operational issues
